headline: Commission sets interview plan for new department director

meeting.voteItem: Motion to go into executive session under HRS 92-5
meeting.summary: The Civil Service Commission set interviews for the 30th and voted to invite DPS employees to take part in the selection process.
meeting.recap: The Civil Service Commission met to finalize the selection process for a new DPS director.[[0:03:10]] A draft schedule set candidate interviews at 10:00, 12:00 and 2:00, with public testimony before each.[[0:05:00]] Commissioners agreed to keep the schedule as prepared and be flexible.[[0:07:09]] The commission voted to go into executive session, a closed-door discussion.[[0:12:08]] Interviews are set for the 30th.[[0:13:59]] DPS staff may send written testimony that will be kept anonymous.[[0:14:06]] Each applicant will give a three-to-five-minute summary statement, then answer questions.[[0:15:16]] The invitation asks DPS employees to watch the interviews live and send anonymous comments afterward.[[0:16:23]] The commission voted to invite DPS employees to take part in the selection process.[[0:17:26]] A commissioner said an earlier call to keep DPS staff out applied only to an earlier stage.[[0:19:00]] The vice chair left during the closed-door session around 11:16 a.m.[[0:21:11]] On October 7, the commission will vote on a pending decision and check for new appeals.[[0:21:46]] A training postponed for six months will go on the November agenda.[[0:22:13]] Commissioners split up the interview questions, with the vice chair taking question two.[[0:24:06]]
decided: The commission voted to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion) with its attorney.
The commission voted to invite DPS employees to be part of the selection process by watching the interviews and sending anonymous written comments.
meeting.next: Staff will draft the invitation email to DPS employees.
